predecessors.name: Tiwanaku Empire
predecessors.text: the Colla Kingdom on the northwest shore of Lake Titicaca (about 20,000 km2 on the page), north of Puno

successors.name: Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu)
successors.text: the Colla Kingdom on the northwest shore of Lake Titicaca (about 20,000 km2 on the page), north of Puno

ledger.x: c. 1150: the Colla Kingdom is established on the northwest shore of Lake Titicaca. Infobox 'c. 1150'; the body only says parts of the Tiwanaku population migrated between 1050 and 1150. Ruled from Hatunqulla by the Zapana dynasty.
1445-1450: Pachacuti defeats the Colla at Ayaviri.
1450: the Colla Kingdom ends and is 'Quechuanized'; revolts under Pachacuti and Tupac Yupanqui follow, and the Altiplano peoples were only fully integrated under Huayna Capac.

wars.name: Colla-Inca war
wars.outcome: Inca victory under Pachacuti (his general Apo Conde Mayta at the border in one version): battle at Ayaviri, Colla chief captured, the Colla and the Lupaca on the northwest shore of Lake Titicaca conquered; Rowe puts the southern border at the Desaguadero…

wars.name: Colla-Lupaca rivalry
wars.outcome: A rivalry placed in the 14th century; under Viracocha Inca the Colla ruler (Cari on the Aymara kingdoms page) invaded Lupaca territory and was defeated at Paucarcolla.

certainty.note: No boundaries on either page; Ayaviri is a battle site.
